definition: A tokenizer-specific unit of model input or output; it may be a word fragment, punctuation or other encoded content.
pm: Do not price a workload from word count alone.

definition: A numeric representation used to encode properties of an item such as text. Similarity depends on the model and task.
pm: Useful for retrieval; similarity is not proof of truth.

definition: A mechanism that combines information from positions in the available context.
pm: A larger context does not guarantee every detail is used well.

definition: A neural-network architecture built around attention and other processing layers; implementations vary.
pm: Know its capabilities and constraints, rather than memorizing diagrams.

definition: Learned numeric values that determine how a model transforms its inputs.
pm: Supplying new documents in a prompt is different from training weights.

definition: Initial training on a broad data mixture to learn general representations and behavior.
pm: Not the same job or cost as calling an existing model.

definition: Running a trained model on current input to produce predictions or outputs.
pm: This is where serving latency and per-request usage arise.

definition: A model-specific capacity for the information processed in a request, subject to input/output and product limits.
pm: Capacity is not a guarantee of recall or a free budget.

definition: A sampling control that changes the relative probabilities used to select outputs, where supported.
pm: Lower variation is not a factual-correctness guarantee.

definition: Designing task instructions, examples and requested output to improve behavior at inference time.
pm: Start with failure examples and a measurable baseline.

definition: Selecting and arranging instructions, history, retrieved evidence and tool results that the model sees.
pm: More context can add noise, cost and contradictory instructions.

definition: Retrieval-augmented generation: provide retrieved evidence as context for generation.
pm: Test evidence retrieval and answer support separately.

definition: Additional training on examples to adapt a model; supervised fine-tuning learns from supplied demonstrations.
pm: Needs data quality, held-out evaluation and supported tooling.

definition: Training that uses preferences or reward signals to shape model behavior. RLHF is one family of methods.
pm: Human preference is not identical to factual truth.

definition: Training a model to learn from another system’s outputs or signals.
pm: Compare quality loss, data rights and serving savings.

definition: Representing model values with lower numeric precision to reduce resource requirements.
pm: Benchmark quality and hardware support for the actual workload.

definition: A procedure for judging outputs or behavior against defined criteria on selected cases.
pm: An eval measures; an intervention changes the product.

definition: Cases reserved from the data used to tune prompts or train the candidate.
pm: Protect it from repeated optimization leakage.

definition: Observable criteria and scoring guidance that define what good looks like.
pm: Calibrate on concrete examples and disagreements.

definition: A model used to assess an output according to a judging task.
pm: Validate against human review and inspect bias.

definition: Unsupported or fabricated generated content, often presented fluently.
pm: Create cases that test evidence support and abstention.

definition: Previously acceptable behavior worsens after a change.
pm: Keep known failures in the regression suite.

definition: Precision concerns the share of selected items that are relevant; recall concerns how many relevant items were found.
pm: Choose the error trade-off based on the user task.

definition: The software around a model that manages context, tools and execution flow.
pm: Reliability depends on the whole system.

definition: A repeated model → action → observation cycle with stopping conditions.
pm: Define budget, recovery and escalation boundaries.

definition: A model requests a structured tool action that the surrounding system handles.
pm: A valid request still needs authorization and error handling.

definition: Model Context Protocol: a standard for connecting compatible applications to tools and data sources.
pm: A connection is not blanket permission or guaranteed relevance.

definition: A property that lets repeated processing of the same operation avoid additional effects.
pm: Important when retries could duplicate consequential writes.

definition: A recorded sequence of inputs, actions, outputs and timing for a run, with appropriate data controls.
pm: Use it to locate the stage that failed or dominated cost.

definition: Reuse of eligible prior prompt processing under a provider’s matching and retention rules.
pm: Check reads, writes, misses and storage before claiming savings.

definition: Time until generation begins returning output; different from total completion latency.
pm: Streaming can change perceived waiting without shortening all work.

definition: The duration at or below which 95% of measured requests complete.
pm: Tail delays can hurt a workflow despite a good average.

definition: Total spend divided by the number of tasks that meet the success definition.
pm: Includes failed attempts, retries and relevant non-model costs.

definition: Model parameter files are available under stated terms; permissions and openness vary.
pm: Check the license, serving cost and maintenance burden.

definition: Applied roles build workflows using models; model-focused roles shape model capability, data, training or platform priorities.
pm: Choose a portfolio project that demonstrates the target role’s decisions.
